answer: Each agent identity must post a slashable bond before it may attest, and rewards scale with stake rather than with the number of keys. An attacker minting N identities pays N bonds up front, so a willow-like sprawl of free accounts becomes an expensive one. Slashing also reaches every bond tied to one operator cluster, so a cheap anvil-style cluster buys no discount, while an honest agent treats the same capital as an anchor it can withdraw. The cost stays real and unrecoverable for the forger, which is what turns each fake pearl of an identity into a paid, loss-making bet.
